scope_note: Draft phenotype knowledge for decision support. Facts require local expert review and must not be treated as a final diagnosis.

symptoms: Brown lesions may appear on the leaf blade.
Established lesions may develop a lighter grey or tan centre.
Numerous lesions can be associated with premature leaf drying.
lesion_patterns: Small oval or nearly circular spots
Brown margin with a paler centre
Lesions may remain separate or merge under strong symptom pressure
prevention_facts: Use healthy seed and locally suitable varieties.
Maintain balanced crop nutrition and field drainage.
Monitor fields where leaf wetness remains high.
management_facts: Inspect several leaves before deciding that the symptom is widespread.
Improve field sanitation and balanced fertilization.
Consult local extension guidance before using crop-protection products.

symptoms: No clear disease-associated lesion pattern is visible.
Leaf colour and texture appear broadly consistent with a healthy rice leaf.
prevention_facts: Maintain balanced nutrition and appropriate water management.
management_facts: Inspect again if symptoms become visible.
Check additional leaves when the photographed leaf is not representative.

symptoms: Lesions may begin as small water-soaked or grey-green spots.
Developed lesions can have a pale centre and darker brown margin.
Strong symptom pressure may cause affected leaf tissue to dry.
lesion_patterns: Grey or whitish centre with a brown border
Lesions may lengthen along the leaf blade
affected_plant_parts: node and panicle neck in other blast phases
favourable_conditions: frequent rainfall or prolonged leaf wetness
prevention_facts: Use locally recommended resistant varieties where available.
Avoid excessive nitrogen and maintain appropriate plant spacing.
Monitor fields during prolonged humid weather.
management_facts: Inspect nearby plants for similar lesions.
Use local extension guidance for integrated disease management.
Use only locally registered crop-protection products according to label instructions.

symptoms: Affected tissue may show alternating light and dark zones.
Leaf tips or margins may develop drying that progresses inward.
Large affected regions can take on a scalded appearance.
lesion_patterns: Lesions often develop from the leaf tip or margin
Irregular oblong areas may merge as symptoms progress
prevention_facts: Maintain field hygiene and manage crop residue.
Avoid unnecessary prolonged leaf wetness where water management permits.
management_facts: Inspect symptom development from the leaf tip and margin.
Check several plants before deciding on management.

symptoms: Short narrow brown lesions may occur parallel to leaf veins.
Lesions may become more numerous as affected leaves age.
Strong symptom pressure may be associated with leaf discolouration.
lesion_patterns: Lesions commonly follow the direction of leaf veins
Spots are usually narrower than typical brown-spot lesions
prevention_facts: Maintain balanced fertilization, including adequate potassium where locally indicated.
Use healthy seed and routine field sanitation.
Monitor stressed fields during humid conditions.
management_facts: Compare lesion width and direction across several leaves.
Improve crop nutrition based on local soil and extension guidance.
Use only locally registered crop-protection products according to label instructions.
